# task\-w02b\-object\-resolution — W02b: commit object resolution and message capture
status: ready  priority: 1  scope: scope-git
readiness: actionable  reason: declared_ready

Accept 7 to 64 hexadecimal characters, resolve them against the selected repository's actual object format, and read that exact object once\. Reject symbolic refs, HEAD, branch and tag names, ranges, revision syntax, ambiguous abbreviations and non\-commit objects, and never peel an annotated tag\. Persist only full lowercase object IDs\. Read the object format, full ID, raw commit message, parent IDs and count, and source checkout context; merge, root, detached\-HEAD and unreachable\-from\-HEAD commits are valid, a bare repository can supply evidence, and no source worktree is reported when absent\. Disable replacement refs so they cannot change the content attributed to an object ID, disable lazy network fetching and interactive prompts, and never run hooks or write into the evidence repository\. Decode the message explicitly and preserve original bytes or encoding metadata when lossless decoding is unavailable\.

## Acceptance
- Full, abbreviated and uppercase inputs resolve to the same full lowercase object ID, while ambiguous, missing, non\-commit and ref\-shaped inputs each produce a distinct coded diagnostic\.
- SHA\-1 and SHA\-256 repositories are both handled where available, and the object format is recorded with the evidence\.
- Replacement refs, a missing promised object, an annotated tag, a merge commit, a root commit and a detached HEAD all behave as specified, and no fetch, hook or write occurs in the evidence repository\.
- Output and time limits produce a clear diagnostic rather than a truncated message or a partially verified object\.
- Stored descriptions are byte\-faithful, including CRLF and non\-UTF\-8 messages, and parser line\-ending normalization never alters them\.
